item.title: Supreme Court to Hear New Case on Race and School Admissions
item.description: The court’s decision to review an admissions policy for selective middle school programs in Maryland follows its rejection of affirmative action in higher education.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow and Abbie VanSickle
item.media:credit: Alex Kent/The New York Times
item.media:description: In 2023, the Supreme Court struck down race-conscious admissions programs at Harvard and the University of North Carolina.

item.title: At Cornell, a Subdued Scene on First Weekend of Fraternity Party Ban
item.description: The moratorium is among the safety measures that the university put in place following the uproar over a former student’s sexual assault lawsuit.

item.media:description: The line outside a popular bar in Ithaca’s Collegetown neighborhood was modest on Saturday night.

item.title: Mamdani to Expand 2-K Program on Staten Island and in the Bronx
item.description: New York City aims to offer 12,000 free child care seats for 2-year-olds next year, including the first spots on Staten Island.
item.dc:creator: Emma G. Fitzsimmons and Matthew Haag
item.media:credit: Angelina Katsanis for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani has said that every 2-year-old in New York City will have a spot in the free child care program by 2029.

item.title: When a Social Media Mob Came for Cornell’s Jane Doe
item.description: After a former student named seven men in a lawsuit saying they had sexually assaulted her, a movement gained steam online to reveal her identity.

item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: A former Cornell student’s lawsuit accusing members of a fraternity of sexual assault stirred anger and debate at the university and on college campuses nationwide.

item.title: School Shooting in Bend, Ore., Has Heroes and Pain, But Few Answers
item.description: The city of Bend, Ore., is praising those who worked to stop the gunman at Silver Rail Elementary School. The authorities are searching for answers.

item.title: Terry Tao Is on the Front Lines of the Debate Over AI and the Future of Math
item.description: The Fields Medalist Terence Tao is on the front lines of a debate about artificial intelligence and the future of his field.
item.dc:creator: Elisabeth Bumiller
item.media:credit: Ariana Drehsler for The New York Times
item.media:description: Terence Tao's celebrated status has made him an unofficial spokesman for mathematics, a job that for now is consuming most of his time.

item.title: Vital Early Voting Period Begins in Texas

item.title: Unrest Mars Day of Protest in France, as Student Movement Turns National
item.description: Riots broke out in several French cities alongside peaceful marches of tens of thousands of people demonstrating against rising living costs and poor school conditions.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Porter
item.media:credit: Jeff Pachoud/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: A tourist office in Lyon, France, that was set on fire during unrest on Saturday. Many rallies stayed peaceful as weeks of student-led protests evolved into a national display of discontent.

item.title: What to Know About the Violent Protests in Albania

item.media:description: A protester faced off with police officers on Saturday during a demonstration in Tirana, Albania.
